sentences.text: 1 P.G. Ajithkumar, J.

This Court as per order dated 16.12.2019 directed the appellant to deposit 50% of the amount due under the impugned award as a condition for stay and permitted the 1 st respondent-claimant to withdraw the amount on such deposit.

The aforesaid order was modified by this Court as per the order dated 12.02.2020, which reads as follows:-
"4. Contention raised is that, the impugned award itself is not maintainable, since the amount of compensation is fixed based on a document which could not have been accepted under provisions of the Act.
We are of the opinion that, even if ultimately the appeal is allowed, it cannot be found that the claimant will not be entitled for any compensation with respect to the property acquired.
The land in question was acquired long back.
Therefore we are of the opinion that the condition insisted for deposit of 50% of the entire amount due under the impugned award, is in no manner illegal or unjustified.
Learned counsel for the petitioner/2nd respondent contended that, if the amount deposited is allowed to be withdrawn unconditionally, that may cause prejudice, if ultimately the appeal is allowed.

Under such circumstances this court may not be powerless to direct re-deposit of the amount, if ultimately if it is found that the claimant is not entitled for compensation even to the tune of 50%
deposited.

However, we think it is only just and proper to direct the 1st respondent/claimant to submit an undertaking before the court below at the time of withdrawal of the amount, to the extent that in the event of this court allowing the L.A. Appeal, and directing re-deposit of the amount withdrawn, the same will be done without any objection."
The appellant preferred Special Leave Petition (C) No.9947 of 2020 against the said order.

The Apex Court disposed of the said S.L.P., which on granting leave filed as Civil Appeal No.4181 of 2023, on 04.07.2023 with the following directions:-
"It is agreed by the learned counsel for the parties that the appellant Kochi Metrol Rail Ltd. will deposit 50% of the enhanced compensation amount in the High Court within a period of six weeks from today.
The deposit would be converted into an interest bearing Fixed Deposit Receipt (FDR) for a period of one year with auto- renewal clause.
The principal amount and interest accrued on the FDR would abide by the orders passed by the High Court.

The direction that 50% of the enhanced compensation amount deposited by the appellant Kochi Metro Rail Ltd., should be released to the respondents, is accordingly set aside and modified in aforesaid terms."
In terms of the said direction, the appellant has produced a cheque bearing No.635798 for an amount of Rs.7,03,77,901/- (Rupees seven crores, three lakhs, seventy seven thousand, nine hundred and one only).
